compiled_from.title: 视觉生成模型 External Evidence：生产级 Model Router Cold-Start Prior 研究报告
compiled_from.why: Carries an explicit operational definition of grades A–D, an explicit version-lock principle, exact-variant Arena entries with sample counts and 95% CI, and a gap/conflict register. Where the two documents disagree this one is taken, because it is the stricter of the two and states the criterion it is being strict about.

compiled_from.title: External Evidence v1 — Primary-Source Verified Final Report
compiled_from.why: A shorter re-verification pass. It discards anything it could not re-check against a primary source, which makes it useful as a corroboration signal and as a record of what one reviewer could not confirm. Its grades are recorded as disagreements rather than merged.

grade_definitions.A: Official or rigorous academic benchmark. Protocol, sample size, model labels and raw results are auditable. May serve as primary external quality evidence.
grade_definitions.B: High-quality independent benchmark or arena. Method is documented and N/CI or sufficient conditions are public, but prompt distribution, unique-rater count or server-side revision are missing. May serve as primary or supporting prior.
grade_definitions.C: Real numbers and some method, but total sample, rater count, CI, prompt corpus or reproduction conditions have important gaps. Weak prior only.
grade_definitions.D: Product capability announcement, marketing material or observational note. Never a quality prior; capability and version metadata only.

version_match_levels.EXACT: Same model version and, where the source pins one, the same revision.
version_match_levels.EXACT_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED_REVISION: Version matches; the source did not pin a revision, so revision attribution stays unspecified.
version_match_levels.VARIANT_MISMATCH: Same version number, different served variant (Veo 3.1 vs Veo 3.1 Fast, Kling Pro vs Standard). Never a prior.
version_match_levels.VERSION_MISMATCH: Different version in the same family (Wan 2.1 vs Wan 2.7). Never a prior, and recorded precisely so nobody re-derives it later.
version_match_levels.MODEL_MISMATCH: A different model entirely (GPT-4o image vs GPT Image 2). Never a prior.

prior_eligibility_rule: grade in {A, B} AND version_match in {EXACT, EXACT_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED_REVISION} AND mapping_confidence != LOW. Everything else is recorded and readable but may not move a routing score.
prohibitions: No normalisation, averaging or ranking across heterogeneous scales (Elo, Likert 1-5, 0-1 automatic, win-rate percentages).
No inheritance of a benchmark result from one model version to another.
No treating a capability claim (30s support, MoE, multi-reference count) as a quality measurement.
Aesthetics is not style_fidelity. Only a test with an explicit target style reference supports style_fidelity.
Compositional alignment (object count, colour, position, attribute binding) is not text_fidelity.
Arena Elo is a holistic preference aggregate and maps to no diagnostic capability.

conflicts.description: The primary document grades the Seedance 2.0 technical report C because overall prompt N, rater N and inter-rater statistics are not public. The cross-check document grades it A, noting the sample total is incomplete and calling it borderline A/B.
conflicts.resolution: C is recorded. The stricter grade is taken because it names the criterion it is applying, and because a weak prior that is labelled weak costs nothing while an overstated one propagates.

conflicts.description: The primary document grades the Veo 3 model card C (sample sizes explicit, raw win rates and rater N absent). The cross-check document grades it A for sample sizes and B for the missing win-rate tables.
conflicts.resolution: C is recorded, for the same reason.

conflicts.description: A figure of 0.976 has circulated for Veo 3.1 Fast on OSCBench. It is the GPT-5.2 *Subject* score, not an aggregate. The cross-check document could not re-verify it from a primary table and excluded it entirely.
conflicts.resolution: Recorded as the Subject sub-metric only. It is not stored as an aggregate and no aggregate is derived from it.

conflicts.description: The cross-check document evidences image generation with GenEval on GPT-4o (Overall 0.84). The primary document evidences GPT Image 2 with Qwen-Image-Bench, PhyEditBench and BizGenEval.
conflicts.resolution: Both are stored. The GenEval record is bound to gpt-image-2 as MODEL_MISMATCH so it can never feed a prior, and exists so nobody re-derives 0.84 onto GPT Image 2.

conflicts.description: On OSCBench, human and GPT-5.2 scores for the same model and dimension differ materially: Veo 3.1 Fast Action .908 human versus .802 automatic; Kling 2.5 Turbo Accuracy .726 versus .652; Wan 2.2 OSC Consistency .668 human versus .710 automatic — the automatic judge is higher in that last case.
conflicts.resolution: Human and automatic scores are stored as separate metrics. Neither is treated as ground truth for the other and they are never averaged.

conflicts.description: The official Lite model card reports a 54.6% T2V win rate against Fast, while the Arena has Lite at 1088 +/-6 and Fast at 1087 +/-6.
conflicts.resolution: Not a contradiction. The Arena CIs overlap almost entirely and the prompt pools and methods differ. A win rate against one opponent must not be converted into an Elo difference.

conflicts.description: Wan-Bench reports Physical Plausibility .939 for Wan 2.1, while independent physics evaluations rank some closed models above Wan 2.1.
conflicts.resolution: Both can hold. Different benchmarks, model pools and definitions of physics. .939 is not a 93.9% real-world physics correctness rate.

conflicts.description: GPT Image 2 scores Physical Plausibility 9.13 on normal physics and 4.85 on anti-physics prompts in the same benchmark.
conflicts.resolution: Not an error. A physics prior must carry its task condition; a single physics scalar per model would be wrong here.

conflicts.description: Seedance 2.0 leads several dimensions in its own SeedVideoBench 2.0 tables while sitting below other models on the current Artificial Analysis holistic leaderboard.
conflicts.resolution: Not the same metric. Internal diagnostic benchmark versus blind holistic preference, different pools, different dates. No fusion into a single score.
